findings: OVERALL: as a body of organic content the three sets do not yet read as one feed. The people set (rows 1-3, indices 1-24) is a coherent, quiet, warm-profile campaign and is the strongest pass so far. The scene set is the weak leg: pass-11 scenes went flat, overcast and vignette-free, so they will not sit next to the A1 post or the E3 guide, and several would read as stock/render to a sceptical patient. The dim set is on-brand and close to F1 and needs only a few culls.

PEOPLE (1-14, band light): confirmed as one campaign. The 6 pass-10 new people (9-14) integrate cleanly with the 8 originals; same wardrobe register (knits, linen, white tees), same inward gaze, same warm wall. Identity holds against originals_8people_contact and pass10 rows 2-3 for every edit I checked. Best of set: 4, 9, 13, 7, 16, 19.
1 platinum woman: confirm keep (7). The band sits on the wall not the face, but it is the closest thing in the set to the E3 guide portrait, which is the brand's hero image, so it earns its place.

3 man with plate: confirm fix, and I would go further: pull it from the organic feed as-is. Full-size view shows a hard-edged light bar starting at the left frame edge, a floating figure with no floor, and a plate-and-cloth prop with no reason to exist. It is the one portrait that reads staged and it breaks the close-crop system the other 31 portraits share. Either re-crop to head-and-shoulders on the band, or drop.

5 dark-haired man slate navy: confirm fix. Right third and both top corners go to black; it reads as the old moody vignette look the brief moved away from. Its lighter sibling 16 is the version to post.

6 long-hair woman 'pearl white': confirm the colour label is wrong (warm greige) but as a brand image it is fine; keep. 9 'charcoal' is actually warm brown and reads as a duplicate slot of 11 - fine for the feed, flag for the pipeline.

8 and 21 East Asian man, hand at face: the oval salon/clinic-chair headrest on the right edge and the disembodied second hand are the only clinical furniture in the whole portrait set. On a hair-transplant account that headrest reads as a barber/clinic chair. Keep 8 as a secondary, but crop tighter on the right to lose the headrest before posting; 21 confirm fix.

10 and 17 South Asian man on 'pearl white': both backdrops are brushed aluminium, not a wall. 10 keep. 17: OVERRULE to keep (7). At full size skin is a plausible warm brown, identity holds, and it is the only 'lighter/hopeful' variant that is actually visibly lighter than its base. Bottom-right corner drop is a small grade fix, not a reshoot.

12 and 24 freckled auburn woman: downcast eyes and closed-in posture read as a 'before' / shame beat, not hope. This is intrinsic to the pass-10 source, not the grade, so no edit fixes it. Keep 12 as a quiet supporting frame, never as a lead; 24 (forest green, darker) I would not post.

15 platinum 'lighter/hopeful charcoal': confirm fix. On the sheet it is indistinguishable from 1 in exposure and the backdrop is olive-brown. 18 Black woman lighter/hopeful: confirm fix, not lighter than 14. Only 16 and 17 delivered the lighter brief.

20 long-hair woman + purple: confirm fix. On the sheet her face is visibly paler and rosier than 6 and than the originals contact; a pink flush on the cheek of a rhinoplasty-account portrait is exactly the healing-flush association we must avoid. Skin lightening is a trust problem, not a taste problem.

PURPLE PEOPLE (19-24) as a set: the mauve is effectively absent in 20-24 and only global-tint in 19, so none of them reads as a purple variant and none has purple on skin. Brand recommendation: retire the purple people variant entirely. The upside (tonal variety in the deep tones) is invisible on a phone and the downside (bruise-reading on a nose) is catastrophic. 19 can be posted as a plain dusty-rose frame.

NEW T2I PEOPLE (25-32): this row does not belong to the same campaign. Six of eight are three-quarter, front-lit, soft-smiling, corporate-headshot poses on smooth painted backdrops; the rest of the set is strict profile, inward, band-lit. It reads like a diversity stock page dropped into an editorial feed. 30 (Scandinavian man, eyes closed) is the one t2i portrait that fully sits with the campaign and is the best single image of the pass (9). 32 (Korean man, eyes closed) also fits (keep). 27 Filipino woman: keep as the one smiling frame that stays calm. 29 mixed-heritage woman: OVERRULE to fix - flat light-grey corporate backdrop, no band, no mood, would look like a LinkedIn headshot in the grid. 31 Chinese woman: OVERRULE to fix - milky high-key, hair painterly, brightest frame in the set. 25, 26, 28: confirm fix (25 too polished/glassy eyes, 26 muslin studio, 28 radial patch). Regenerate the six as profiles, eyes down or closed, on the band-lit wall, shirt/knit wardrobe only.

SCENES (33-64) as a set: confirm the per-image pattern. Almost every frame is missing the A1 corner darkening and has gone cool/overcast, so the scene set is visibly brighter and greyer than the people set and than the A1 post. Pass-7 (v3 contact row 3) is warmer, has corner falloff and sunset light, and is still the quality bar; pass-11 regressed. The other structural problem is repetition: the same hotel suite appears five times (33, 34, 39, 51, 57), the same SUV four times (35, 36, 52, plus 61 interior), the same suitcase three times (37, 38, 53). A feed needs distinct moments, not six grades of one prop list.

39 confirmed LABEL MISMATCH: full-size view is the hotel suite (bed, tray, roses, green velvet chair, Bosphorus window), not balcony tea. 40 is the balcony tea. Pipeline index is off by one in that pair.

45 and 54 'clinic consultation room': both are the same hotel-bedroom armchair corner with a framed Galata print. Nothing about them reads clinic, which is actually the safer failure for the brand (no anything clinical), but the prompt is not landing. Confirm 45 fix and 54 kill; if a consultation room is needed, brief it as a quiet sitting room (like 58) rather than a clinic.

35, 36, 52 chauffeur SUV: confirm fix; 35 also has the water glass on the pavement and a cropped foot (people rule). 37, 38, 53 airport suitcase: all three carry readable Turkish Airlines tail livery through the glass - a hard logo fail for a brand that cannot imply an airline partnership. Confirm fix/kill on all three; a real fix means a different window view or a crop that loses the apron.
43 and 44 Galata cafe: confirm kill. Saturated pastel postcard, staged tea-glass pair, repeating bollards; it is the most 'travel-stock' frame of the pass and would undermine trust the fastest.

Scene keeps that actually read as photographs: 59 recovery-day room (best scene of the pass, glasses on the bed, cardigan, slippers, real fabric), 58 sitting room, 63 last-morning room, 50 entryway (with hardware fixes), 55 car back seat. 61 car interior: OVERRULE to keep-with-crop (7) despite the prompt mismatch. It is the most convincing phone photograph in the entire pass (rain on glass, worn leather) and that realism is precisely what this account lacks; apply the corner darkening and a warmer grade, crop the far-left window strip where distant terminal signage sits, and it is postable. 47 airplane Portra is the only edit with corner darkening at roughly the right dose but the tray-table geometry is wrong; confirm fix.

Scene method ranking observed on the sheet: the new t2i scenes (57-64) outperformed the edits of pass-7 scenes (33-50), because the edits re-staged the identical props and stripped the warmth. Of the six 'realism' styles, Lived-in Portra (59, 47) came closest to the brand, Phone candid was high-variance (61 excellent, 43 worst), Hotel's own photo produced brochure frames except 63, Open daylight produced 58 but otherwise flat, Plain photo control added nothing over the source, and Wide off-axis deep focus (36, 42, 48, 60) was the worst: everything-sharp render look every time. Purple scenes (51-56) mostly turned into global lilac casts (52, 54, 56); only 55 kept mauve in the blacks.

DIM (65-80) as a set: confirm the per-image verdicts broadly; this is the most on-brand of the three sets and would carry white serif copy well. 66, 68, 69, 70, 72, 74, 77, 78 are ready. 65 and 73 palms are near-symmetric but read as the F1 slide-1 backdrop and will work under copy.

The backdrop colour instruction drifted on about a quarter of frames (charcoal rendered warm brown in 9, 15, 22; pearl white as putty in 6). The lighter/hopeful step did not work: 15 and 18 are darker than their bases, 16 is only marginally lighter, 17 lifted the wall and the skin together. Next pass: dark walls only, G1 polarity (face lit, wall darker, brightest only in a feathered zone at eye height), and do the lighter variant as a masked numeric grade with a pass/fail luminance check.
syn.purple_verdict: Retire it on people and scenes. On people the purple step produced zero mauve (dark-pixel B-G between -4.9 and +0.5 on all six), so the hard-fail criterion is trivially met (no purple on any face) but 19-24 are duplicates of their base frames; the upside is invisible on a phone and the downside on a rhinoplasty account is a bruise read, so the variant is not worth its risk. On scenes only 52, 55 and 56 carry a trace and 51/53/54 none; where it was visible it drifted toward midtone casts rather than plum in the blacks. Keep purple only as a dim-backdrop option (73 and 74 are the proof it can work there) applied through a strict luminance mask (L under 25, low saturation) so it never reaches midtones as it did in 75, 76, 79 and 80.
syn.dim_verdict: Strongest and most on-brand set of the pass. 66, 68, 72, 73, 74 and 77 are ready behind white serif copy now (86-98% of pixels under L40, one residual light area kept to a corner), with 65, 69, 70 and 78 as usable spares. Two corrections for the whole set: the cast is amber-brown rather than the warm-neutral F1 asks for (desaturate the warm 20-30%, most on 70, 77, 78), and the residual light area must stay in a corner and under about L70 (79 and 80 breach this). Scene-like dims fail as backdrops: 67 (one-point corridor, light dead centre, reads horror) is killed, 71 (hammam arch) and 76 (archviz courtyard) survive only with crops and colour fixes. Blur works; 77 is the better blur because 78 is nearly a black card.
spec_changes: PEOPLE band edit: restrict the band-light backdrop palette to charcoal, slate navy, forest green and deep warm brown; drop pearl white, peach, stone grey and light dusty rose from the band set (or lower their base value by one stop) because the band reads as a stage stripe on light walls.

PEOPLE band prompt: 'soft light falls on the face at eye level; the wall behind is darker than the face and lightens only in a feathered horizontal zone at eye height, easing to dark within the top and bottom 15-20% of the frame; no defined edges, sides not darkened, wall and face lit from the same direction'. Negative: light bar, stripe, gradient overlay, spotlight, vignette.

PEOPLE lighter/hopeful: implement as a numeric grade, not a prompt: +0.5 to +0.7 stop on the wall and shadow side with a skin mask; accept only if wall mean L rises by 15 or more versus the base and face mean L changes by 3 or less. Re-run 15, 17, 18 this way.
PEOPLE purple: drop the variant entirely (19-24 produced no mauve; risk of bruise read). Do not re-run.
PEOPLE backdrop colour gate: measure the wall hue/luminance against the label before review and reject drift (charcoal came out warm brown three times, pearl white as putty).

PEOPLE new t2i: strict profile or three-quarter-back, eyes down or closed, closed mouth, no smile with teeth, knit/linen/white-tee wardrobe, band-lit dark wall, real pore texture; negative: studio muslin, corporate headshot, catchlight, smile, flat front light. Cap eyes-closed head-tilted poses at one in four so the set does not cluster into a 'recovery' read (10, 17, 30, 32 already exist).

PEOPLE re-edits: 3 (man with plate) re-edit from source as a head-and-shoulders crop with the plate and cloth removed; 8/21 (hand at face) inpaint the second hand and the oval headrest out or crop right 25%; 6 desaturate the malar flush before posting.

SCENES route: abandon edits of pass-7 seeds; generate every scene by t2i on the 57-64 route, one frame per moment, no duplicate seeds (pass 11 had five hotel suites, four SUVs, three suitcases). Aim for 18 distinct moments in the patient's week.

SCENES vignette: apply the A1 corner darkening as a numeric post step, target corner/centre luminance ratio 0.50-0.60 (A1 measures 0.37-0.48 x 0.8), asymmetric and following the light source rather than a radial overlay, verified per frame before review; 47 is the dose reference.

SCENES light: specify 'low warm late-afternoon or lamp light through the window, soft shadows, held highlights' and forbid 'overcast, flat, grey, HDR'; the pass-7 suite (v3 contact row 3 col 1) remains the bar and is warmer AND darker-cornered than anything in pass 11.

SCENES realism cues in every prompt: lived-in detail (glasses on the bed, cardigan on the chair, slippers, unmade linen), imperfect surfaces, subject off-centre, 35mm/phone depth falloff, no more than two props. Negative list: tray with roses, tea glass as hero, sugar cubes, arranged towel stack, framed prints, stacked landmarks, sun disc.

SCENES hard-rule prompts: airport frames face inward or use frosted glass (no apron or tail-fin view); car frames are interior or three-quarter front with no tailgate, badge or wheel-cap; no signage, plates or door numbers; no people or body parts.
SCENES presets: drop Wide off-axis deep focus and Plain photo; use Lived-in Portra and Hotel's own photo as the two styles; Phone candid only on t2i.
SCENES consultation room: re-brief as a quiet sitting room in the manner of 58 (two chairs, window, carafe), never a clinic; 45/54 produced hotel corners, which is the safer failure but not the ask.
SCENES pipeline: fix the index slip that labelled the hotel suite as balcony tea (39/40) and the prompt drift on 61 (interior instead of kerb) and 64 (flat-lay instead of morning counter).

DIM: desaturate the warm cast 20-30% toward warm-neutral across the set; keep the one residual light area in a corner (top-left or bottom-right) under L70; keep the centre 60% of the frame under L40; no corridors, arches, pools with sconces or pillar bands through the copy area; blur variants with a single light source. Dim purple only through a luminance mask (L under 25, saturation 8% or less).

REVIEW gates before human review: automated logo/text detector, person/body-part detector, corner/centre ratio, wall hue versus label, face delta L versus base, dark-pixel B-G for purple; anything failing a gate is regenerated, not reviewed.
syn.summary: Pass 11's people set is the strongest so far: identity holds on all 24 edits, no purple reached any face, and ten portraits (30, 4, 9, 13, 7, 16, 14, 11, 10, 1) can post as one campaign. The band light only works where the wall is dark and the face carries the highlight; on pale walls it reads as an applied stripe, the lighter/hopeful step did not lighten (15 and 18 are darker than their bases, 17 lifted the skin), and the purple step produced zero mauve, so both variant families are duplicates and the purple people variant should be retired. Six of the eight new t2i portraits are three-quarter corporate headshots that break the profile campaign; only 30 (best image of the pass) and 32 fit, so 25-29 and 31 need regenerating as band-lit profiles. Scenes regressed: the corner darkening was not applied on 25 of 32 frames, the light went overcast and grey, the edits restaged seven pass-7 seeds as near-duplicates, and 37/38/53 (airline livery), 35/36/52 (badges, cropped foot), 43/44 and 54 are hard kills; only the t2i route produced photographs (59, 58, 63, 57) plus the 55 back seat. The dim set is on-brand and ready behind white serif copy (66, 68, 72, 73, 74, 77 selected), needing only a 20-30% pull on the amber cast, with 67 killed and 71/75/76/79/80 fixable by crop and colour. Pass 12 should keep the band-light edit on dark walls only, do the lighter variant as a masked numeric grade, drop purple except as a luminance-masked dim option, rebuild every scene by t2i with a verified corner ratio of 0.50-0.60, warm low light and lived-in detail, and add automated logo/person/skin-luminance gates before human review.
